primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Donohue syndrome due to biallelic INSR pathogenic variants
mechanism: INSR encodes the insulin receptor, a transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinase. Severe loss of insulin-receptor function causes profound insulin resistance with hyperinsulinemia, fasting hypoglycemia/postprandial hyperglycemia, growth restriction, and characteristic somatic findings.
vignette: A 4-month-old infant has severe prenatal and postnatal growth restriction, very little subcutaneous fat, hypertrichosis, acanthosis nigricans, and organomegaly. Laboratory studies show extreme hyperinsulinemia, fasting hypoglycemia, and postprandial hyperglycemia. Molecular testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in INSR.
lead: The receptor affected in this patient belongs to which of the following signaling-protein classes?
distractors: Cytokine receptor that signals through JAK-STAT proteins
Membrane receptor with intrinsic serine/threonine kinase activity
distractor_notes: The insulin receptor is not a seven-transmembrane GPCR; it is a heterotetrameric transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinase.
JAK-STAT signaling is used by many cytokine and growth-hormone-family receptors, whereas INSR has intrinsic tyrosine-kinase activity.
Steroid and thyroid hormone receptors are examples of intracellular ligand-activated transcription factors; insulin signals through a cell-surface receptor.
Intrinsic serine/threonine kinase activity characterizes receptors such as TGF-β receptors, not the insulin receptor.
key_expl: INSR encodes the insulin receptor, a transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinase. Severe biallelic INSR dysfunction causes Donohue syndrome, with profound insulin resistance and hyperinsulinemia despite fasting hypoglycemia and postprandial hyperglycemia, together with severe growth restriction and characteristic physical findings.
objective: Identify the insulin receptor as a transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinase and connect severe biallelic INSR dysfunction with Donohue syndrome.
